items.rationale: The window holds everything the model reads and writes for the call: instructions, tool descriptions, history, tool results and the reply. Picking a shows only the messages are counted; c and d confuse the window with training or with other chats (M3).
Nothing persists between sessions unless the program saves it and loads it into the next context. Window size does not carry over, and the manuals do not hold a student's status.

Call 1 reads 1,050. Call 2 reads 1,050 + 50 + 200 = 1,300. Call 3 reads 1,300 + 50 + 300 = 1,650. Total 1,050 + 1,300 + 1,650 = 4,000. An answer of 1,650 counts only the last call, as if the model remembered the earlier ones (M3).
Retrieval puts only the relevant pages in context, so cost stays low and recall is better. Sending everything costs tokens each call and degrades recall; a bigger window is not the fix.

Saving findings as notes, clearing old tool results and keeping a summary (compaction) reduces cost and context rot while keeping progress. A larger window keeps the clutter (M4); restarting loses the work; the model does not remember better than the input it is given (M3).
